suite.title: Mid-air text entry with four virtual keyboards in VR

study.title: Mid-air text entry with four virtual keyboards in VR
study.researchQuestion: How do four virtual keyboards for mid-air text entry in VR (a raycast QWERTY keyboard, a drum-like keyboard, a swipe gesture keyboard and a split keyboard) differ in entry speed, uncorrected errors, entry time per phrase, perceived workload, arm and shoulder comfort and preference?
study.agentQuestions: The forecasts are made before the study, from what is known in advance; no measured outcome is ever an input. Which configurations reproduce the human differences between the keyboards: the brief alone, the brief with a background note on text entry, or the brief with the cohort's background? Does knowing a person's background help to forecast that person? Does another model, given the same, forecast differently?

runtime.deviceProfile: Meta Quest 3 with two controllers (hand tracking off); no runnable app in this suite

outcomes.label: Entry speed
outcomes.description: (|T| - 1) / S x 60 / 5 per phrase, with T the transcribed phrase and S the seconds from the first key (or gesture) to Enter; a word is five characters. Mean over the ten scored phrases per participant and keyboard.

outcomes.label: Uncorrected error rate
outcomes.description: Errors left in the submitted phrase: the minimum string distance between presented and transcribed phrase divided by the longer of the two. Errors corrected before Enter do not count. Mean over the ten scored phrases.

outcomes.label: Entry time per phrase
outcomes.description: Seconds from the first key (or gesture) to Enter; a phrase not finished after 180 s is ended. Geometric mean over the ten scored phrases, because times are right-skewed. In one family with entry speed, so the two share one weight.

outcomes.label: Workload (raw NASA-TLX)
outcomes.description: Raw (unweighted) NASA-TLX after each keyboard: six items on 0-100 scales in steps of 5; the score is their mean. Lower means less workload; for performance, 0 = perfect and 100 = failure.

outcomes.label: Arm and shoulder comfort
outcomes.description: Single item after each keyboard: 'My arms and shoulders felt comfortable while typing with this keyboard' (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree).

outcomes.label: Preference rank
outcomes.description: After all four keyboards: 'Which keyboard would you choose to enter text in VR?', ranked from 1 (first choice) to 4, without ties.
